conventions.landmarkAge: age REACHED by building the landmark. The fandom Scots page lists landmarks under the age they are BUILT in (Dark Age: Abbey of the Isles / Stone of Destiny); we normalise to age reached. Official page confirms Stone of Destiny = Feudal, Tower of Skye = Castle, Dhùn Èideann = Imperial.
conventions.region: Lowlands / Highlands matters: Mustering Hall technologies from a region get 'greatly reduced' cost once a Landmark of that region is built. Region is stated officially only for Stone of Destiny (Lowlands), Tower of Skye (Highlands), Dhùn Èideann (Lowlands); the other three are inferred as the opposite region of their pair.
conventions.confidence: official = ageofempires.com / Steam store text; wiki = ageofempires.fandom.com (Scots page expanded 2026-10-10 'new info from civ page reveal' and 2026-10-22 by 'Geer of War', no stated source for the landmark/tech lists); community = forum / third-party; inferred = our reading

bonuses.name: Highland Wealth
bonuses.text: Start the game with a Highland Cattle, which generates food over time as it grazes at Berry Bushes. Official page: 'The Scots Dark Age begins with assigning their first Highland Cattle to Berry Bushes near a Tower House'.

bonuses.name: Highland Cattle grazing
bonuses.text: Highland Cattle graze at Berry Bushes for bonus Food over time WITHOUT depleting them. Trickle rate, cattle cost and train time unknown. Tower Houses produce and shelter (garrison) cattle.

bonuses.name: Highland Ambush
bonuses.text: Infantry gain increased movement speed while in Stealth Forests and do not receive any vision penalty (official: Scots infantry 'see directly through' Stealth Forests). Clan Traditions extends the bonus duration.

bonuses.name: Tower House replaces Outpost
bonuses.text: Tower Houses act as Outposts, increase population capacity, produce Highland Cattle and give cattle unique garrison spaces. Can have an attached barmkin to bring cattle inside. Cost/pop amount unknown.

bonuses.name: Mustering
bonuses.text: Mustering Hall musters warriors rapidly by spending Food on 'muster charges'; military buildings within its influence improve mustering. Holds Lowland and Highland technologies that 'greatly reduce in cost' when a Landmark from that region is constructed. Celebrating-2026 post: 'a quick way to field units at a discount'. Charge cost, unit counts and cooldowns unknown.

bonuses.name: Fishponds
bonuses.text: Kirkmen create and gather Gold from Fishponds; while Kirkmen work Fishponds, nearby Villager gather rates are also increased. Unlocked by Stone of Destiny (Feudal). Fishpond limit raised by Stew Ponds.

bonuses.name: Starting conditions
bonuses.text: Start with one Highland Cattle (above). Otherwise standard start assumed; starting resources not stated.

landmarks.name: Abbey of the Isles
landmarks.effect: Contains a Saint's Relic that provides an area healing aura. The relic (with its aura) can be transferred to other buildings to additionally increase that building's research and production speed.
landmarks.region: Highlands (inferred: pair of Stone of Destiny)

landmarks.name: Stone of Destiny
landmarks.effect: Buildings constructed within its reach have part of their construction cost refunded as Gold ('feudalization'). Grants early access to Kirkmen (and Fishponds). Rebate percentage unknown.

landmarks.name: Snowdoun Gate
landmarks.effect: Produces infantry for free (rate/which units unknown).
landmarks.region: Lowlands (inferred: pair of Tower of Skye)

landmarks.name: Tower of Skye
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Tower House with added emplacements and generates a surrounding Stealth Forest. Grants other Tower Houses the ability to generate Stealth Forests and increases infantry damage by 15% in Stealth Forest.

landmarks.name: Dhùn Èideann
landmarks.effect: Defensive landmark with seven cannon attacks ('Seven Sisters'). Produces gunpowder siege engines at lower cost and with increased range.

landmarks.name: Three Loch Lookout
landmarks.effect: Acts as a Mustering Hall with large line of sight. Adds extra muster charges and increases warriors received per muster. Can muster ships if built near water.

uniqueUnits.name: Highland Cattle
uniqueUnits.notes: Livestock. Tasked to Berry Bushes to generate a Food trickle without depleting the bush. One at game start. Garrisons in Tower Houses (Barmkins adds slots). Fermtouns and Pastures raises its gather rate.

uniqueUnits.name: Pikeman
uniqueUnits.age: Dark ('Pictish Pikeman stands ready' in Age 1 text)
uniqueUnits.notes: Spearman variant with significantly increased melee range. Forms the schiltron with Men-at-Arms (Lochaber Axes) and Gallowglass.

uniqueUnits.name: Cateran
uniqueUnits.building: Barracks (inferred; fandom commented-out infobox says Barracks/Feudal)
uniqueUnits.notes: Swift light melee infantry; bonus damage vs workers and buildings (torching). Basket-Hilted Broadswords (Imperial) boosts attack speed/damage; Cateran's Trail gives speed aura and forest healing.

uniqueUnits.name: Gallowglass
uniqueUnits.notes: Heavy melee infantry with claymore; area-of-effect damage; can brace against cavalry charges. Fandom S&W: strong vs archers, horsemen, spearmen; weak vs crossbowmen.

uniqueUnits.name: Border Reiver
uniqueUnits.building: unknown (Celebrating-2026 post: musterable at Mustering Hall)
uniqueUnits.notes: Light ranged gunpowder cavalry with pistols and torches; counters ranged cavalry; raids perimeters. Affected by Snaphance Locks.

uniqueUnits.name: Kirkman
uniqueUnits.building: unknown (religious; early access via Stone of Destiny; Stew Ponds spawns one)
uniqueUnits.notes: Religious unit that creates Fishponds and gathers Gold from them; boosts nearby Villager gather rates while working.

uniqueUnits.name: Ghillie
uniqueUnits.notes: Scout variant that can enter stealth at any time.

uniqueUnits.name: Highland Archer
uniqueUnits.notes: Archer variant with increased damage but less range.

uniqueUnits.name: Tacksman
uniqueUnits.notes: Handcannoneer variant that enhances damage of nearby highland warriors.

uniqueUnits.name: Man-at-Arms (standard, with Lochaber Axes)
uniqueUnits.notes: Not unique, but Lochaber Axes gives +damage and brace vs cavalry; named in official schiltron text.

uniqueBuildings.name: Tower House
uniqueBuildings.effect: Defensive building (acts as Outpost); provides population space; produces and garrisons Highland Cattle; barmkin attachment for cattle; with Tower of Skye can generate Stealth Forests. Fortified Tower Houses adds fire armor; Barmkins adds cattle garrison slots.

uniqueBuildings.name: Mustering Hall
uniqueBuildings.produces: Mustered warriors for Food (muster charges); Gallowglass from Castle; Border Reivers per Celebrating-2026 post
uniqueBuildings.effect: Technology building holding Lowland/Highland unique techs (cheaper once matching-region Landmark built). Military buildings in its influence improve mustering. Three Loch Lookout acts as a larger one.

uniqueBuildings.name: Fishpond
uniqueBuildings.effect: Harvestable gold source that also improves resource gathering of nearby workers. Limit exists (raised by Stew Ponds).

uniqueTechnologies.name: Barmkins
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Tower Houses gain increased garrison slots for Highland Cattle.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Basket-Hilted Broadswords
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases attack speed and damage of Caterans.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Birlinn Crews
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Galleys gain increased movement speed and attack speed.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Cateran's Trail
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Caterans increase movement speed of nearby infantry; infantry heal while out of combat and in Stealth Forests.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Clan Traditions
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases melee infantry damage and the duration of their Highland Ambush bonus.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Fermtouns and Pastures
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Villagers gather faster from Farms; Highland Cattle gather faster from Berry Bushes.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Feuds Aside
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases attack speed of gunpowder units.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Fortified Tower Houses
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Tower Houses gain increased fire armor.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Lion's Duty
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Infantry gain increased armor near landmarks and defensive buildings.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Lochaber Axes
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Men-at-Arms gain increased damage and can brace against cavalry charges.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Snaphance Locks
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Replaces Serpentine Powder with the same effect, also affecting Border Reivers.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Stew Ponds
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Instantly spawns a Kirkman and increases Fishpond limit; further increases gather rates of workers near Fishponds.

uniqueTechnologies.name: Wallace's Rally
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases infantry production speed; newly created infantry get a large temporary movement speed buff.

uniqueTechnologies.name: We Stand Alone
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Increases building health and emplacement attack speed; buildings regenerate HP.

uniqueTechnologies.name: 'Seven Sisters' cannons
uniqueTechnologies.effect: Landmark cannon emplacements plus increased gunpowder siege range (landmark effect, not a researched tech).

economyNotes.text: Food: start with one Highland Cattle grazing Berry Bushes (non-depleting trickle). More cattle come from Tower Houses. Rate per cattle, cattle cost/time, cattle cap and Tower House cost are all unpublished, so the food curve cannot be modelled yet. The Malian cattle precedent in the installed catalog (90 gold, 15 s) is NOT evidence for Scots values.
Gold: Stone of Destiny (Feudal, Lowlands) refunds part of nearby building costs as gold and unlocks Kirkmen/Fishponds (gold source + nearby gather-rate aura). Percentages unknown.

Military-for-food: Mustering Hall converts Food into muster charges that spawn warriors rapidly; Snowdoun Gate (Castle) produces infantry for free. Both substitute for normal production costs; values unknown.
Tower House replaces Outpost AND adds population, so house count may be partly replaced by Tower Houses; whether normal Houses still exist is not stated.
Generic 17.0 change affecting all civs: Town Center construction time 150 -> 165 s. No general age-up cost changes in the 17.0 preview.
Age-up and landmark costs, starting resources: not published; standard values would be an assumption.

openingsCommentary.summary: Official 'Through the Ages': Age 1 - task the starting cattle to berries near a Tower House, build Tower Houses for pop + cattle production; Pikemen defend. Age 2 - Stone of Destiny (Lowlands), build inside its reach for gold rebate, Kirkman + Fishpond, build Mustering Hall and spend Food on muster charges. Age 3 - Tower of Skye (Highlands) for Stealth Forests, Gallowglass from Barracks/Mustering Hall. Age 4 - Dhùn Èideann, Border Reivers, Basket-Hilted Broadswords, final Mustering Hall techs. Note this showcases a Lowlands-Highlands-Lowlands path, which would pay full price for one region's techs in Feudal/Castle.
Steam / 17.0 notes framing: 'resilient and defensive', 'thrive in prolonged battles', Mustering Hall lets you lean Highland (aggression) or Lowland (defense).
Official forum threads (286737 and 207081) contain only reactions and speculation (e.g. 'Scots are just another variant', unit-name guesses from screenshots); no stats or openings.
